title: The Man Who Moved After Stillness
dek: American actor and disability advocate who turned life after a 1995 spinal-cord injury into a public fight for paralysis research, access, and dignity.
mortality_event: 1995 equestrian accident causing paralysis from the neck down; afterward he used celebrity to build spinal-cord research and quality-of-life advocacy before his death in 2004.
citation_passage: Christopher Reeve (1952–2004) was an American actor, director, and advocate for people living with paralysis. Known internationally for playing Superman, he sustained a spinal-cord injury in a riding competition on May 27, 1995. After rehabilitation, he used his public profile to press for research funding and better quality of life for the paralysis community. His creative work continued: he directed In the Gloaming and published the autobiography Still Me. This six-page biographical comic follows the injury and the work that came afterward, including advocacy, research support, and efforts to make disabled people's needs heard in public life.
